name: scale-map
title: Scale map
tagline: Gridded map with a compass rose, landmark icons, a scale bar and a double number line; distances and 8-point directions between places are derived from the scale and occludable.
description: A gridded map (a square grid with North up) carrying named landmarks, with measured-distance arrows between them, a graphical scale bar, a compass rose, and an optional double number line pairing map squares to real distance — the primary "read a map with a scale" model. You author the map: the grid size, where each landmark sits (at grid coordinates [col, row]), the scale ("1 square represents 2 km"), and which landmarks each arrow joins. The model derives every measured quantity — each arrow's real distance (its grid length × the real distance per square; exact for straight-across and right-angled-route legs), its eight-point compass direction (N, NE, E, …), the scale statement, the scale-bar label and every number-line value. An arrow can run straight between two landmarks ("as the crow flies") or follow a right-angled route through waypoints ("along the roads"). Each arrow can show its distance, its direction, both or neither, and occlude the readout for a "how far / which way?" question. Occlude a landmark's name, or the compass points, for labelling questions. The grid is the measuring tool, so the scale bar drawn under it is true to the squares on screen.
whenToUse: Reach for this for primary map-and-scale work: reading a map, counting squares to measure a distance, "how far is the school from the park?", "which direction is the pond from the well?", and using a scale or a double number line to convert squares to real distance. Author the map and let everything measured derive. Set the grid (grid: { cols, rows }) and the scale (scale: { real, realUnit } reads "1 square represents <real> <realUnit>"; add square to say "<square> squares represent <real> <realUnit>" — e.g. square 2, real 1, realUnit "km"). Place landmarks at grid coordinates ([col, row], measured from the bottom-left corner, so North is +row / up): each takes an id, a label (the place name), and an icon from the set (pin, home, school, tree, church, shop, pond, mountain, flag, star — use pin for anything else; the label carries the meaning, the icon is decoration). Draw arrows between landmarks (arrows: [{ from, to }]); each arrow's real distance and compass direction are derived — set show to "distance", "direction", "both" or "none". For a route along the roads rather than straight across, give via: a list of [col, row] corner points the arrow bends through (its distance is the sum of the legs). Common configurations: worked — arrows show "both" so the distance and direction both read; question — occlude an arrow ("?") and pose it in the caption ("how far is it?"); answer space — occlude every arrow and show the number line so pupils convert for themselves; directions — arrows show "direction" and the compass occluded ("label the compass; which way is each place?"); conversion — give a numberLine to make the square↔real proportion explicit, marking and occluding one value. The scale bar (scaleBar) shows by default and is true to the squares; the compass rose (compass, default 4-point top-right) shows by default — turn either off with show:false, or set compass.points to 8. Put the rose in a corner with no landmark (compass.position), so the two do not overlap. Keep the same scale and the same grid across the blocks of one lesson so pupils read one map. A staged build reads well: open on the labelled map, add an arrow per stage, reveal the worked distance last (the base map stands alone). Synonyms a teacher might use: map, scale, map scale, scale & maps, read a map, distance on a map, how far, compass, compass directions, north east south west, points of the compass, grid, squares, double number line, key, treasure map, route.

grid.description: The map's square grid — the measuring tool. Landmarks sit at grid coordinates [col, row]; arrow distances are counted in these squares. Keep the same grid across the blocks of one lesson.

cols.description: Number of columns of squares (the grid is cols wide). The map is drawn to a fixed pixel width whatever cols is, so the squares shrink as cols grows.

rows.description: Number of rows of squares (the grid is rows tall, North at the top).

showLines.description: Draw the faint square gridlines. Default true — pupils count the squares, so usually keep them on.

scale.description: The scale — what one square of the grid represents in the real world. Every distance, the scale statement, the scale bar and the number line derive from it. "1 square represents <real> <realUnit>" by default; set square for "<square> squares represent <real> <realUnit>".

real.description: The real-world distance that `square` square(s) represent, in `realUnit`. With square 1, realUnit "km": real 2 reads "1 square represents 2 km".

realUnit.description: Unit of `real`, and the unit every derived distance is shown in.

square.description: How many grid squares represent `real`. Default 1 (the usual "1 square represents …"). Set to e.g. 2 for "2 squares represent 1 km" (each square is then half a km).

statement.description: Show the scale statement in words ("1 square represents 2 km") above the scale bar. Default true.

landmarks.description: The named places on the map. Each sits at a grid coordinate; the position is the only authored geometry (a map's layout is original content — there is nowhere to author a distance). Arrows reference landmarks by id.

id.description: Short unique identifier used by arrows to reference this landmark (e.g. "school", "park"). Kebab-case.

at.description: Grid coordinate [col, row] of the landmark, from the BOTTOM-LEFT corner: col 0 is the left edge, row 0 the bottom edge, and row increases UPWARDS (North). [3, 4] is 3 squares right and 4 squares up. Must lie within the grid (0..cols, 0..rows).

label.description: The place name drawn beside the icon (e.g. "School", "Harbour"). The label carries the meaning; the icon is decoration.

icon.description: Which map symbol to draw. "tree" reads as a park/wood, "pond" as water, "mountain" as a hill, "flag"/"star"/"pin" as a generic marker. Use "pin" for anything not in the set — the label names it. Default "pin".

occlude.description: Render this landmark's label as "?" — the "name this place" hook. The icon stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw this landmark in amber — the place in focus or the answer. Default false.

arrows.description: Measured-distance arrows between landmarks. Each arrow's real distance (grid length × the real distance per square) and its 8-point compass direction are DERIVED — never authored. Straight from→to by default; give `via` for a right-angled route along the roads.

from.description: id of the landmark the arrow starts at.

to.description: id of the landmark the arrow ends at.

via.description: Optional corner points [col, row] the arrow bends through — a route "along the roads" instead of straight across. The distance becomes the sum of the legs (from → via[0] → … → to). Use right-angled corners so the legs count whole squares. Omit for a straight "as the crow flies" arrow.

show.description: What to label on the arrow: "distance" ("6 km"), "direction" (the compass direction "East"), "both" ("6 km, East"), or "none". Default "distance".

occlude.description: Render the arrow's readout as "?" — the "how far / which way?" hook. The arrow stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the arrow and its readout in amber — the answer or the leg in focus. Default false.

style.description: "solid" (default) for a measured/travelled leg; "dashed" for a route or reference shown alongside a straight one (e.g. the along-the-roads route next to the straight distance).

compass.description: The compass rose drawn in a corner of the map. Shown by default (4-point). Set show:false to hide it.

show.description: Draw the compass rose. Default true.

points.description: 4 for N E S W, or 8 to add NE SE SW NW. Default 4.

position.description: Which corner of the map the rose sits in. Default "top-right".

occlude.description: Hide the compass labels other than N as "?" — the "label the compass" hook (North is always shown as the map's orientation). Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the rose in amber emphasis. Default false.

scaleBar.description: The graphical scale bar drawn under the map (a segmented ruler labelled with the real distance). True to the squares on screen — the grid is the measuring tool. Shown by default.

show.description: Draw the scale bar. Default true.

squares.description: How many grid squares long the bar is (its end label is squares × the real distance per square). Default: a sensible fraction of the map width.

numberLine.description: Optional double number line beneath the map making the square↔real conversion explicit: a top line ticked in squares (0, 1, 2, …) over a bottom line ticked in the real distance. Omit for no number line; include it for conversion-focused teaching.

show.description: Draw the number line. Default true when the object is present.

upTo.description: The largest number of squares on the line (it runs 0..upTo). Default: enough to cover the longest arrow.

mark.description: Ring one conversion on the line to focus on it.

squares.description: The squares value to ring (its real partner is shown beneath).

occlude.description: Hide the real value at the mark as "?" — "how many <unit> is this?". Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the mark in amber. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the map; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. the fact being taught. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
